name: Besan Chilla
steps: Finely chop the tomato, capsicum and coriander so the pieces will sit within a thin pancake. Mix gram flour, cumin, turmeric and salt in a bowl.
Whisk in water gradually, first making a smooth paste and then loosening it to a pourable batter. Scrape the sides of the bowl to remove dry flour pockets.
Fold in the chopped vegetables and coriander and rest for 5 minutes. The batter should spread from a ladle without running like water; add a small splash of water if it becomes too thick.
Heat a non-stick or well-seasoned tawa over medium heat and brush lightly with some of the measured oil. Pour a ladle of batter into the centre and spread gently into a thin circle.
Cook for 2–3 minutes until the top loses its wet sheen, the edges lift and the underside is golden. Loosen around the edge with a flat spatula before flipping.
Cook the other side for 1–2 minutes until no wet batter remains. Repeat with the remaining batter and oil, adjusting the heat if the outside browns before the centre cooks.
tips: Keep vegetable pieces small so the chilla flips cleanly.
substitutions: Any substitution changes the recipe: recheck allergies, Jain rules and quantities.
notes: Ingredient costs are estimates. Check local prices before shopping.
